story.title: Shooting Victim from 2024 Trump Rally in Butler Passes Away
story.summary: James Copenhaver, 76, who was shot during an assassination attempt at a Trump campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, has died from complications related to his injuries. The shooting also resulted in the death of another individual and grazed Trump's ear with a bullet. Trump expressed his condolences, calling Copenhaver's death a 'tremendous loss.'

explore_lenses.label: How severe were Copenhaver’s injuries?
explore_lenses.title: Long-term injuries preceded his death
explore_lenses.summary: Copenhaver survived the July 13, 2024 shooting but lived with serious, lasting injuries for more than two years. Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said he died from complications of those wounds, though public reporting has not provided a medical examiner’s detailed cause-of-death finding.

claims.text: Copenhaver was struck in the arm and abdomen during the Butler rally shooting; reporting on his federal lawsuit says the injuries required multiple surgeries and left lasting kidney, leg-sensation and other impairments.
Attorney General Dave Sunday said Copenhaver had been gravely wounded and died from complications stemming from those injuries.
Local reporting said the Allegheny County medical examiner confirmed he died in hospital but had not publicly released a cause of death.

Local reporting said the Allegheny County medical examiner confirmed he died in hospital but had not publicly released a cause of death.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The public record reviewed does not include a medical examiner report detailing the precise medical mechanism linking the 2024 injuries to his death.

explore_lenses.label: What did investigations find went wrong?
explore_lenses.title: Reviews identified preventable security failures
explore_lenses.summary: Official reviews did not attribute the attack to one isolated mistake. They found overlapping planning, communication, staffing and perimeter-security failures that left the nearby AGR complex and roof insufficiently secured.

claims.text: The bipartisan House task force concluded the Butler attack was preventable and said failure to secure the adjacent American Glass Research property created vulnerabilities that allowed Thomas Crooks to reach the roof and fire.
The Secret Service’s independent review panel found that no federal, state or local personnel were specifically assigned to secure the AGR building, roof or surrounding area.

A later GAO review, released through the Senate Judiciary Committee, found failures to share threat information, unclear operational roles, resource shortcomings and communication problems; GAO made eight improvement recommendations.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen to the Copenhavers’ lawsuit?
explore_lenses.title: A pending federal negligence case may need updating
explore_lenses.summary: Before his death, Copenhaver and his wife filed a federal tort suit alleging that Secret Service failures caused their life-altering injuries. The case’s current docket status and any amended claims or estate substitution were not publicly verifiable from the records reviewed.

claims.text: James and Marianne Copenhaver filed their federal tort action on June 1, 2026, against the U.S. Department of Justice in the Western District of Pennsylvania; the docket shows it was assigned to Judge Christy Criswell Wiegand and placed in alternative dispute resolution.

Their reported position is that the United States Secret Service and Department of Homeland Security failed to provide appropriate rally security, and that Copenhaver’s physical and emotional injuries resulted from that negligence; these are allegations, not court findings.
The publicly indexed docket reviewed was last retrieved in early June 2026, so it does not establish what procedural action, if any, followed Copenhaver’s September 23 death.

story_report.summary: James Copenhaver, who was shot at Donald Trump’s 2024 campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, has died from complications related to his injuries. The shooting was part of an assassination attempt on Trump. Copenhaver’s death adds a fatal consequence to an attack that injured rally attendees and prompted multiple official reviews of the security operation. His pending federal lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Justice had alleged that federal security failures contributed to his physical and emotional injuries.

sections.heading: Copenhaver’s Injuries and Medical Treatment
sections.body: Copenhaver was struck in the arm and abdomen during the Butler shooting. Reporting on his federal lawsuit said he underwent multiple surgeries and was left with lasting impairments involving his kidneys, leg sensation and other functions. Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said Copenhaver had been gravely wounded and died from complications stemming from those injuries.

sections.heading: Butler Security Reviews Identify Failures
sections.body: A bipartisan House task force concluded that the attack was preventable, finding that failure to secure the adjacent American Glass Research property created vulnerabilities that enabled Thomas Crooks to reach a roof and fire. An independent Secret Service review panel found that no federal, state or local personnel had been specifically assigned to secure the building, its roof or the surrounding area. A later GAO review also cited failures in threat-information sharing, operational roles, resources and communications, and issued eight recommendations.

sections.heading: Copenhaver Lawsuit Remains Procedurally Unclear
sections.body: James and Marianne Copenhaver filed a federal tort action against the Justice Department on June 1, 2026, in the Western District of Pennsylvania. The case was assigned to Judge Christy Criswell Wiegand and placed in alternative dispute resolution. The Copenhavers alleged that the Secret Service and Department of Homeland Security failed to provide appropriate rally security; those claims were allegations rather than court findings.

unresolved.text: Local reporting said the Allegheny County medical examiner confirmed that Copenhaver died in a hospital but had not publicly released a cause of death. The reviewed record does not include a medical examiner report detailing the precise medical mechanism linking his 2024 injuries to his death.

The publicly indexed docket reviewed does not establish what action followed Copenhaver’s death, including whether the complaint will be amended, an estate representative substituted or additional death-related damages sought.

related_stories.summary: A powerful explosion in the Plaka district of Athens, near the Acropolis, caused a two-storey building to collapse on September 25, 2026. At least two people were injured in the incident. The cause of the explosion is under investigation, with a gas leak suspected.
